findings.title: Use === and !==, never == or !=
findings.message: Replace loose equality operators with strict equality. Lines 13, 16, 19, 22, 25 use == or != instead of === or !==, which can lead to unexpected type coercion bugs.

claims.claim: Line 13 in src/checkout.js uses == instead of ===
claims.reason: The diff shows that line 13 was changed from `if (order.status === "pending")` to `if (order.status == "pending")`, confirming the use of == instead of ===.

claims.claim: Line 16 in src/checkout.js uses != instead of !==
claims.reason: The diff shows that line 16 was changed from `if (order.couponCode !== null)` to `if (order.couponCode != null)`, confirming the use of != instead of !==.

claims.claim: Line 19 in src/checkout.js uses == instead of ===
claims.reason: The diff shows that line 19 was changed from `if (order.user.role === "admin")` to `if (order.user.role == "admin")`, confirming the use of == instead of ===.

claims.claim: Line 22 in src/checkout.js uses != instead of !==
claims.reason: The diff shows that line 22 was changed from `if (order.tier !== "free")` to `if (order.tier != "free")`, confirming the use of != instead of !==.

claims.claim: Line 25 in src/checkout.js uses == instead of ===
claims.reason: The diff shows that line 25 was changed from `if (order.shippingMethod === "express")` to `if (order.shippingMethod == "express")`, confirming the use of == instead of ===.

claims.claim: Loose equality operators can lead to unexpected type coercion bugs
claims.reason: The rule document explicitly states: 'Loose equality performs type coercion that hides bugs ("0" == false, null == undefined, etc.).' This directly supports the claim that loose equality can lead to unexpected type coercion bugs.

claims.claim: Strict equality operators (=== and !==) should be used instead of loose equality operators (== and !=)
claims.reason: The rule document title and content explicitly state 'Always use strict equality' and provide examples of replacing == with === and != with !==. This directly supports the claim.
